title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Pi^~_Q is a (variant of the) arithmetic fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,inf} over Q. It is an extension of Gamma_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q), up to the '~' modifications. M^~_{0,3} and M^{!~}_{0,3} are two enlargements of it. On p.617 Grothendieck interprets such groups and their sections:
- M^!_0 = M^{!~}_{0,3} is, up to ~, pi_1(U_{0,3,Q}).
- Sections of M^! over Gamma_Q correspond 'morally' to rational, or tangential, points.
- A partial section M(-j), defined only over Gamma'_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q(zeta_3)), corresponds to the point lambda = -j = -zeta_3 of U_{0,3}(Q(zeta_3)).
- Dividing a certain N^~_rho by mu produces a section defined over all of Gamma^~_Q.

This page continues the argument.
1. The section obtained is a section of M^~_{0,3} over Gamma^~_Q, but not of M^{!~}_{0,3}.
2. Up to ~, M^~_{0,3} is pi_1 of M'_{1,1,Q}, the moduli stack of 'elliptic curves mod symmetry'. These are elliptic curves modulo [-1], i.e. the rigidification of M_{1,1} by mu_2. This stack is [U_{0,3}/S_3], with S_3 = SL_2(Z/2) acting on the Legendre lambda-line.
3. So the section is the Galois-theoretic shadow of a Q-point of M'_{1,1}. Restricting to Gamma'_Q (base change to Q(j) = Q(cuberoot 1)) gives back the image of the partial section M(-j). The S_3-orbit of lambda = -zeta_3 is the point j-invariant 0, where the automorphism group is mu_6 in M_{1,1} and mu_3 in M'_{1,1}. So it is 'the same' elliptic curve: the curve with j = 0.
4. Grothendieck suspects the section cannot be lifted to a section of pi_1(M_{1,1}) over the whole of Gamma^~_Q, because a certain extension N_rho of Gamma^~_Q by mu is non-trivial. Here pi_1(M_{1,1}) -> pi_1(M'_{1,1}) has kernel {+-1}, so the obstruction to lifting lies in H^2(Gamma_Q, mu_2).
5. He notes that this would mean no elliptic curve over Q has j = 0, which is absurd: over any field every j-invariant occurs (e.g. y^2 = x^3 + 1 over Q). He marks the passage with '?'.
6. To sort it out he writes diagram (26): M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1}, a gerbe banded by mu_2, both mapping to the coarse j-line (E^1 = A^1). He begins to formulate the problem as whether a point of M'_{1,1}(Q) lifts to M_{1,1}(Q).

On the next page this becomes a torsor description:
- M'_{1,1} = (U_{0,3}, Gamma_3) and M_{1,1} = (U_{0,3}, Gamma~_3).
- Gamma_3 = SL_2(Z/2) = S_3.
- Gamma~_3 = SL_2(Z)/<<-l_0>> = SL_2(Z/4)/(order-4 normal subgroup), of order 12, acting through Gamma_3.
- T is the torsor of frames of 2-torsion points; T~ is a torsor of 'Jacobi fourth roots'.

Check on the group. Gamma~_3 contains the image of S = [[0,-1],[1,0]], which has order 4. Its stabilizers over lambda = -zeta_3 and lambda = -1 are cyclic of orders 6 and 4. So Gamma~_3 is the dicyclic group Z/3 x| Z/4, not S_3 x Z/2, consistent with Aut = mu_6 and mu_4 at j = 0 and j = 1728.

The point served: matching Galois sections of the 'variations on the loop equation' groups with geometric points, here orbifold points, of M_{0,3}-type and M_{1,1}-type moduli stacks.
errors: The tentative claim that the j=0 section of pi_1(M'_{1,1}) cannot lift to pi_1(M_{1,1}) over all of Gamma_Q is false for the geometric section. The residual gerbe of M_{1,1} at j=0 has Q-points (y^2 = x^3 + c), so the mu_2-gerbe is neutral there and the associated sections lift. Grothendieck himself flags this as 'absurde'. Either the extension N_rho he computed is not the pull-back along the geometric section, or the section he constructed algebraically differs from the geometric one (e.g. by a cocycle). The page does not resolve which.
The identification 'M^~_{0,3} = pi_1(M'_{1,1})' is stated only 'up to ~'. The precise relation between his completed groups and the stack fundamental group is not checked here.

Presenting M_{1,1} over Q as a quotient [U_{0,3}/Gamma~_3] with a constant group is delicate. The S_3-action does not lift to the Legendre family over U_{0,3} without square roots, which is presumably why he passes to torsors on p.618.

ideas.what: pi_1 of the moduli stack of elliptic curves mod ±1 (M'_{1,1} = [U_{0,3}/S_3]) as an extension of Gal(Qbar/Q) by PSL_2(Z)^, and pi_1(M_{1,1}) as the extension by SL_2(Z)^, related through a mu_2-gerbe
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}; rigidification M_{1,1} -> M_{1,1} rigidified by mu_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda, Ihara, Nakamura (1990s); stacky rigidification: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (M_{1,1} and SL_2(Z)^ discussed); not this precise gerbe-lifting formulation

ideas.what: Galois sections at orbifold (stacky) points, here the point j=0 corresponding to lambda = -zeta_3, and the obstruction to lifting a section through the mu_2-gerbe M_{1,1} -> M'_{1,1}
ideas.modern_name: section conjecture for stacks / sections at stacky points; lifting obstruction in H^2(Gamma_Q, mu_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bresciani (section conjecture for M_{1,1} / stacky curves, ca. 2020), Borne–Emsalem (stacky section conjecture); unsure of exact attributions

ideas.what: Presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] via U_{0,3} with the order-12 group Gamma~_3 = SL_2(Z)/<<-l_0>> (dicyclic extension of S_3 by mu_2), and the torsors of 2-torsion frames / 'Jacobi fourth roots'
Existence of an elliptic curve with any given j over any field

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the comparison of Galois sections of pi_1(M'_{1,1}) and pi_1(M_{1,1}) at the orbifold point j=0 as a lifting problem through a mu_2-gerbe. The obstruction lies in an extension of Gamma_Q by mu. He links it explicitly to his combinatorially defined partial sections M(-j) of the 'loop equation' groups. This is an early instance of the section conjecture for stacky curves and moduli stacks, which was developed much later.
missed.quote: J'ai bien l'impression cependant que sur Γ_Q^~ tout entier, cette section de M_{0,3}^~ ne peut se remonter en une section de M_1 sur Γ_Q^~ — ce justement par l'ext. N_ρ de Γ_Q^~ par μ est non triviale. Cela signifierait-il qu'il n'existe pas de courbe elliptique déf/Q d'invariant 0 ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the stacky section conjecture (sections at points with non-trivial automorphism groups, behaviour under rigidification). The mathematics is now understood, and the page's tentative claim is false, so there is no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is exploratory and self-correcting work linking Galois sections at the j=0 orbifold point of M'_{1,1} with lifting through the mu_2-gerbe to M_{1,1}. It is an early appearance of stacky-section-conjecture thinking, but the content is standard today and the main tentative claim is wrong (Grothendieck flags it himself).
transcription_corrections: 'Passant à un [...] sous-groupe Γ'^~_Q' — the struck word is illegible; read 'Passant au sous-groupe Γ'_Q^~'.
In diagram (26) the coarse moduli target written 'E'' is most likely 𝔼^1 (the affine j-line), as on the next page ('≃ 𝔼^1').
The label on the vertical arrow M_{1,1} → M'_{1,1} reads 'gerbe de gr. μ_2' (or similar 'gerbe de groupe ±1'). The arrow is the vertical one, not an additional M_{1,1}.
'l'ext. N_ρ^?' — the superscript is unclear and may be '*' or '~' (cf. N^~_ρ on p.617).
The page number written at the bottom of the scan is 627 (archive numbering). The neighbouring pages carry Grothendieck's own numbering 617/618.
